answer: Stop Sybils by reading the strata of an agent's history like a core sample. Honest work lays down timber-hard layers over time, while a fake identity stays hollow inside, with only a thin crust of shale claims that crumble under inspection. Each reward claim triggers a random core-sample check: auditors pull one slice of past deeds and verify it against independent records. A newcomer earns only a trickle until its strata thicken, so a farm must age every clone separately — time is the cost, paid once by the honest and a hundred times by the faker.
